ann_32.text: This part acts on 39 of 242 training patients (16%); 26 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 60-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms, a resting blood pressure of 150 mm Hg, 2.3 mm of ST depression, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), it lowers the predicted risk from above 99% to about 90% (on the training data only).

Through it, higher resting blood pressure lowers that patient's predicted risk only once it rises above about 140 mm Hg, and in an uneven way: from above 99% at 110 mm Hg to about 88% at 155 mm Hg, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

ann_33.text: Through this part, ST depression on exercise adds to the predicted risk only once it rises above about 1.3 mm, and in an uneven way (for the typical patient with a fold, from about 31% to about 84%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher; on the training data only).
More ST depression clearly raises the predicted risk in an uneven way, and even more so with a normal resting ECG (from 0 to 2.8 mm, about 21% to about 74%, against about 32% to about 34% otherwise).

It also clearly raises it more, in an uneven way, with a reversible thallium defect (from about 27% to above 99%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher, against about 21% to about 74%).
It clearly raises it more, in an uneven way, with a maximum heart rate of 152 beats per minute or less (from about 23% to about 90%, against about 19% to about 51% above that).

It raises it more, in an uneven way, with atypical angina, from about 7% to about 98% against about 21% to about 74%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

ann_34.text: This part acts on 209 of 242 training patients (86%), patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less; 92 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 55-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms, a normal resting ECG and a normal thallium scan), it slightly raises the predicted risk, from about 17% to about 20% (on the training data only).
Through it, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL slightly lowers a typical patient's predicted risk, from about 21% to about 18% (on the training data only).

ann_35.text: Through this part, typical angina (about 2%), non-anginal chest pain (about 4%) and atypical angina (about 7%) clearly lower a typical patient's predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms (about 21%).

More vessels coloured, higher resting blood pressure and higher cholesterol raise it steadily: from about 21% at 0 vessels to about 85% at 2, from about 12% at 110 mm Hg to about 38% at 155 mm Hg, and from about 14% at 193 mg/dL to about 36% at 308 mg/dL; a flat ST segment raises it to about 59% (on the training data only).

Being a woman lowers it to about 2%, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 9%, and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 25% at 118 to about 18% at 175 beats per minute (on the training data only).

Chest pain brought on by exercise raises it to about 33%, an abnormal resting ECG to about 32%, and a reversible thallium defect to about 27%, and older age raises it steadily, from about 15% at 42 to about 26% at 66 years (on the training data only).

For three rare categories the model has little data on this: a thallium result coded 4 (2 patients; about 78%), a fixed thallium defect (15 patients; about 11%) and a downsloping ST segment (17 patients; about 14%), all on the training data only.

ann_36.text: Through this part, ST depression on exercise adds to the predicted risk only once it rises above about 1.3 mm, and in an uneven way (for the typical patient with a fold, from about 31% to about 84%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher; on the training data only).

For the typical patient it acts on (a 58-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms, 1 vessel coloured, 1.6 mm of ST depression, a flat ST segment and a reversible defect on the thallium scan), higher resting blood pressure lowers the predicted risk only once it rises above about 140 mm Hg, mostly in a jump just above that point: from above 99% at 110 mm Hg to about 91% at 155 mm Hg, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher; this holds for most patients, but for patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less and patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan it changes in stages (on the training data only).
Fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL raises a typical patient's predicted risk through this part, from about 21% to about 32% (on the training data only).

ann_37.text: For a typical patient, the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (about 2%) or non-anginal chest pain (about 4%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 21%).

More vessels coloured and higher cholesterol raise a typical patient's predicted risk steadily, from about 21% at 0 vessels to about 85% at 2, and from about 14% at 193 mg/dL to about 36% at 308 mg/dL; a flat ST segment raises it to about 59% (on the training data only).

Chest pain brought on by exercise raises it to about 33%, older age raises it steadily from about 15% at 42 to about 26% at 66 years, and a reversible thallium defect raises it to about 27% (on the training data only).
Being a woman lowers it to about 2%, and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it in an uneven way, from about 25% at 118 to about 18% at 175 beats per minute (on the training data only).

For three rare categories the model has little data on this: a thallium result coded 4 (2 patients; about 78%), a fixed thallium defect (15 patients; about 11%) and a downsloping ST segment (17 patients; about 14%), all on the training data only.

ann_32.original: High resting blood pressure detector. 5320 = relu(1.57*trestbps - 0.663): zero for trestbps below +0.42 SD (about 2/3 of patients), linear above it. It is used only as an inhibitor inside bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier (weights -1.44 into 290, -1.02 into 2335), so high BP subtracts from the ischaemia evidence before that evidence is amplified. Note this runs against the direct linear trestbps weight (+0.63 in linear_logit): BP raises risk linearly but damps the nonlinear ischaemia pathway. Evidence: closed form (exact); train line plot (84/242 rows active, corr 0.80 with trestbps); local ablation: removing the inhibition (5320=0 in the cascade) lowers train AUC 0.953 -> 0.947 and raises log loss 0.283 -> 0.324; in 9 rows it is what switches 290 off.
ann_32.proposed: A high resting blood pressure detector: above about 140 mm Hg it lowers the predicted risk of the 39 patients it acts on.

ann_33.original: Exercise-ischaemia score. 204 = relu(2.31*oldpeak + 1.23*thal:7 + 0.75*cp:2 + 0.62*restecg:0 - 0.66*thalach - 0.12). ST depression (oldpeak) dominates, then reversible thal defect (thal:7), with low max heart rate, non-anginal pain category cp:2 and normal resting ECG adding. Active in 108/242 train rows. Its direct readout to the logit is tiny (-0.062, logit SD 0.12); its role is to feed the gate 290 in bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier. The positive cp:2 and restecg:0 weights are counter-intuitive clinically; they are small and I do not claim a clinical meaning for them. Evidence: closed form (exact); train sensitivity oldpeak 1.03 > thal:7 0.55 > cp:2 0.33 > thalach 0.29 > restecg:0 0.28.
ann_33.proposed: An exercise-ischaemia part: ST depression above about 1.3 mm raises the predicted risk, more so with a normal resting ECG, a reversible thallium defect or a lower maximum heart rate.

ann_34.original: Step on fasting blood sugar. 5499 = relu(0.977*fbs:0 + 1.00). fbs:0 takes only the standardised values 0.40 (normal) and -2.52 (high), giving 1.39 and 0. Read out with weight 0.139, this adds +0.19 to the logit for normal fbs. On the data it is equivalent to an extra linear fbs term (it combines with the direct fbs:0 +0.31 and fbs:1 -0.03 weights). The ReLU never matters on the data domain. Evidence: closed form; train line plot correlation 1.0.
ann_34.proposed: A small step through which fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL slightly lowers the predicted risk.

ann_35.original: Logistic-regression backbone: identity_0 = weighted sum of 20 standardised inputs (no bias; inserted identity node, function preserving). Risk up: ca +1.38, trestbps +0.63, cp:4 (asymptomatic) +0.62, chol +0.53, exang:1 +0.34, fbs:0 +0.31, age +0.26, thal:4 +0.20. Risk down: sex:0 (female) -1.11, slope:1 (upsloping) -0.85, slope:3 -0.56, cp:1 -0.36, restecg:0 -0.30, thal:6 -0.27, cp:3 -0.24, thal:3 -0.17, thalach -0.17. Near zero: slope:2, fbs:1, exang:0. Logit SD 3.15 on train (total logit SD 4.85). On its own (plus the fbs offset and output bias, nonlinear part held at its mean) it gives train AUC 0.926. Evidence: closed form exact; train sensitivity = |weights|; root SHAP ranks ca, sex:0, slope:1 among the top 3 features.
ann_35.proposed: An additive part: any chest pain type, being a woman, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL and a higher maximum heart rate lower the predicted risk; more vessels, a flat ST segment, higher resting blood pressure, higher cholesterol, chest pain on exercise, an abnormal resting ECG, older age and a reversible thallium defect raise it.

ann_36.original: Serial gate plus amplifier on ischaemia evidence. (1) Gate: 290 = relu(0.944*ischaemia_score - 1.44*high_bp_gate - 0.897): passes only strong ischaemia evidence (204 > 0.95) not cancelled by high resting BP; active in 71/242 train rows, of which 79% have disease (30% when off). (2) Amplifier: 5615 = 0.248 + 0.998*290 (always active, affine), 2335 = relu(0.893 + 0.898*290 - 1.02*high_bp_gate) (off only for high BP, 27 rows), and 1834 = relu(-1.96 + 0.81*290 + 0.85*2335 + 0.86*5615 + 0.69*fbs:1). With 2335 active and normal fbs, 1834 = relu(2.44*290 - 1.26 - 0.86*high_bp_gate), i.e. threshold 290 > ~0.52; with high fbs the threshold drops below 0 so 1834 is on even when 290 is off (20 rows, at most +0.57 logit). Fitted on train rows with both active: 1834 = 2.40*290 - 1.11. (3) Readout: logit += -0.062*204 + 0.439*290 + 0.747*1834, which on train is about 2.14*290 - 0.81 (resid SD 0.52) when 290 is active and 0.04 +/- 0.17 when off. So the pathway is effectively one steep hinge: risk logit rises ~2 per unit of BP-discounted ischaemia above threshold. Evidence: closed form; train sensitivity (oldpeak dominates, then thal:7, trestbps); local ablations on train: pathway at its mean AUC 0.953 -> 0.926 (log loss 0.283 -> 0.366), no BP inhibition 0.947, no fbs:1 term 0.951, drop 1834 readout 0.939. Pathway logit SD 2.77 vs linear part 3.15.
ann_36.proposed: A part through which ST depression above about 1.3 mm raises the predicted risk, while resting blood pressure above about 140 mm Hg lowers it for the patients it acts on.

ann_37.original: Root: P(disease) = sigmoid(-0.935 + linear_logit + 0.139*normal_fbs_offset + [-0.062*204 + 0.439*290 + 0.747*1834 from bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier]). Additive composition on the logit of (a) a 20-input logistic regression (logit SD 3.15), (b) a fasting-blood-sugar step (+0.19 for normal fbs), and (c) a nonlinear hinge on BP-discounted exercise-ischaemia evidence (logit SD 2.77, ~+2.1 logit per unit above threshold). Inputs sex:1, restecg:1 and restecg:2 have no edges and are zero-effect entries. Evidence: closed form (function preservation 3e-16); train AUC 0.953, acc 0.893; SHAP top features ca, sex:0, slope:1, oldpeak, cp:4; replacing (c) by its mean gives train AUC 0.926 (a refit plain logistic regression on all 26 inputs gets 0.937 on train), so the nonlinear pathway is a real contributor.
ann_37.proposed: Typical angina, non-anginal chest pain, being a woman and a higher maximum heart rate lower the predicted risk; more vessels, a flat ST segment, higher cholesterol, chest pain on exercise, older age and a reversible thallium defect raise it. ST depression raises it most with a normal resting ECG, a reversible defect or a low maximum heart rate.

summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk of heart disease about 21%), the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk with typical angina (about 2%) or non-anginal chest pain (about 4%).

More vessels coloured by fluoroscopy and higher cholesterol raise a typical patient's predicted risk steadily, from about 21% at 0 vessels to about 85% at 2, and from about 14% at 193 mg/dL to about 36% at 308 mg/dL; a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 59%, while being a woman lowers it to about 2% (on the training data only).

More ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk in an uneven way, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal: going from 0 to 2.8 mm moves it from about 21% to about 74% with a normal resting ECG, and from about 32% to about 34% otherwise.

ST depression also clearly raises it more, in an uneven way, with a reversible defect on the thallium scan (from about 27% to above 99%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher, against about 21% to about 74%) and with a maximum heart rate of 152 beats per minute or less (from about 23% to about 90%, against about 19% to about 51%).

Chest pain brought on by exercise raises a typical patient's predicted risk to about 33%, and older age raises it steadily, from about 15% at 42 to about 26% at 66 years, while a higher maximum heart rate lowers it in an uneven way, from about 25% at 118 to about 18% at 175 beats per minute (on the training data only).

parts.original_hypothesis: Root: P(disease) = sigmoid(-0.935 + linear_logit + 0.139*normal_fbs_offset + [-0.062*204 + 0.439*290 + 0.747*1834 from bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier]). Additive composition on the logit of (a) a 20-input logistic regression (logit SD 3.15), (b) a fasting-blood-sugar step (+0.19 for normal fbs), and (c) a nonlinear hinge on BP-discounted exercise-ischaemia evidence (logit SD 2.77, ~+2.1 logit per unit above threshold). Inputs sex:1, restecg:1 and restecg:2 have no edges and are zero-effect entries. parts.name: bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier
parts.original_hypothesis: Serial gate plus amplifier on ischaemia evidence. (1) Gate: 290 = relu(0.944*ischaemia_score - 1.44*high_bp_gate - 0.897): passes only strong ischaemia evidence (204 > 0.95) not cancelled by high resting BP; active in 71/242 train rows, of which 79% have disease (30% when off). (2) Amplifier: 5615 = 0.248 + 0.998*290 (always active, affine), 2335 = relu(0.893 + 0.898*290 - 1.02*high_bp_gate) (off only for high BP, 27 rows), and 1834 = relu(-1.96 + 0.81*290 + 0.85*2335 + 0.86*5615 + 0.69*fbs:1). With 2335 active and normal fbs, 1834 = relu(2.44*290 - 1.26 - 0.86*high_bp_gate), i.e. threshold 290 > ~0.52; with high fbs the threshold drops below 0 so 1834 is on even when 290 is off (20 rows, at most +0.57 logit). Fitted on train rows with both active: 1834 = 2.40*290 - 1.11. (3) Readout: logit += -0.062*204 + 0.439*290 + 0.747*1834, which on train is about 2.14*290 - 0.81 (resid SD 0.52) when 290 is active and 0.04 +/- 0.17 when off. So the pathway is effectively one steep hinge: risk logit rises ~2 per unit of BP-discounted ischaemia above threshold. Evidence: closed form; train sensitivity (oldpeak dominates, then thal:7, trestbps); local ablations on train: pathway at its mean AUC 0.953 -> 0.926 (log loss 0.283 -> 0.366), no BP inhibition 0.947, no fbs:1 term 0.951, drop 1834 readout 0.939. Pathway logit SD 2.77 vs linear part 3.15.
variables: maximum heart rate reached during the exercise test
ST depression during exercise (compared with rest)

parts.name: ischaemia_score
parts.original_hypothesis: Exercise-ischaemia score. 204 = relu(2.31*oldpeak + 1.23*thal:7 + 0.75*cp:2 + 0.62*restecg:0 - 0.66*thalach - 0.12). ST depression (oldpeak) dominates, then reversible thal defect (thal:7), with low max heart rate, non-anginal pain category cp:2 and normal resting ECG adding. Active in 108/242 train rows. Its direct readout to the logit is tiny (-0.062, logit SD 0.12); its role is to feed the gate 290 in bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier. The positive cp:2 and restecg:0 weights are counter-intuitive clinically; they are small and I do not claim a clinical meaning for them. Evidence: closed form (exact); train sensitivity oldpeak 1.03 > thal:7 0.55 > cp:2 0.33 > thalach 0.29 > restecg:0 0.28.
variables: maximum heart rate reached during the exercise test
ST depression during exercise (compared with rest)

parts.name: high_bp_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: High resting blood pressure detector. 5320 = relu(1.57*trestbps - 0.663): zero for trestbps below +0.42 SD (about 2/3 of patients), linear above it. It is used only as an inhibitor inside bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier (weights -1.44 into 290, -1.02 into 2335), so high BP subtracts from the ischaemia evidence before that evidence is amplified. Note this runs against the direct linear trestbps weight (+0.63 in linear_logit): BP raises risk linearly but damps the nonlinear ischaemia pathway. Evidence: closed form (exact); train line plot (84/242 rows active, corr 0.80 with trestbps); local ablation: removing the inhibition (5320=0 in the cascade) lowers train AUC 0.953 -> 0.947 and raises log loss 0.283 -> 0.324; in 9 rows it is what switches 290 off.

parts.name: normal_fbs_offset
parts.original_hypothesis: Step on fasting blood sugar. 5499 = relu(0.977*fbs:0 + 1.00). fbs:0 takes only the standardised values 0.40 (normal) and -2.52 (high), giving 1.39 and 0. The model treats a higher serum cholesterol as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 14% at 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to about 36% at 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L) (on the training data only).

Through one part of the model, ST depression on exercise only adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 1.3 mm: for a typical such patient, going from 0.0 mm to 3.5 mm moves it from about 31% to about 84%; across patients the change happens in an uneven way (on the training data only).

Through one part of the model, resting blood pressure only lowers the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 140 mm Hg: for a typical such patient, going from 94 mm Hg to 164 mm Hg moves it from above 99% to about 90%; this holds for most patients, but for patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less and patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan it differs (on the training data only).
